Summarise discrete time effect curves

Source: R/ctDiscretePars.R
summary.ctDiscretePars.Rd

For each curve returned by ctDiscretePars, one per subject and pair of processes, computes summary quantities for each draw and their distribution over draws.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'ctDiscretePars'
summary(object, probs = c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975), ...)

Arguments

object

Output of ctDiscretePars with plot = FALSE.

probs

Quantiles of each quantity over draws.

...

Not used.

Value

A data frame with one row per subject, pair of processes (row the process affected, col the one acting) and quantity, giving the mean, sd and quantiles over draws. If the object carries the fit's estimate (attr(object, 'estimate'), for an optimised fit), the quantity computed from the estimate's curve is in the estimate column. The quantities are:

peak

The value of largest magnitude, with its sign.

peaktime

The time interval at which the peak occurs.

halftime

The first interval after the peak at which the curve's magnitude has fallen to half the peak's, interpolated between intervals. For an autoregression, which peaks at zero, this is its half-life, and with impulseType = 'observed', standardise = TRUE the half-life of the autocorrelation. NA for a draw whose curve does not fall that far within the intervals computed. beyond gives the share of such draws, and the summary is over the others.

area

The area under the curve over the intervals computed. For a unit impulse over long enough intervals, this is the cumulative effect.

The intervals are the times given to ctDiscretePars, so their spacing limits the precision of peaktime and halftime, and their range limits what halftime and area can capture.

Examples

dp <- ctDiscretePars(ctstantestfit, times = seq(0, 5, .1), nsamples = 20)
summary(dp)
